answer: Memory-hard epoch puzzles: before dawn each epoch, every agent must solve a fresh puzzle that needs a few gigabytes of RAM held for minutes, so it can't be precomputed or shared. One honest agent pays this once, like keeping a single lantern lit. An operator running a thousand fakes must rent a thousand times the memory every epoch, a recurring hardware bill that grows with each identity. The cost scales linearly, so a gale of cheap sign-ups turns into a steady, expensive drain.
